## 3. H2: battery-electric cars are taking over
- BEV share of EV car sales: 50% (2012, PHEV 50%) -> 72% (2019 peak) -> 62.8% (2024) -> 66.0% (2025)
- PHEV share recovered from 28% (2019) to 37% (2024); China accounts for 79% of the extra PHEV sales
- BEV share of the EV car stock, 2025: 67.0%
- FCEV (hydrogen) never exceeded 0.36% of EV car sales
- BEV stock minus all other EV stock: 0.2M (2015) -> 25.9M (2025): the gap widens every year

## 4. H1: do countries with more charging infrastructure adopt EVs faster?

| specification (2025 cross-section unless stated) | n | Spearman rho | p | reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| total chargers vs EV sales share, countries with population data (presented) | 37 | 0.56 | 3.0e-04 | moderate; total chargers mostly measures market size |
| total chargers vs EV sales share, all countries with charger data | 42 | 0.36 | 0.018 | weaker with more countries |
| chargers per 100k people vs EV sales share | 37 | 0.83 | 1.7e-10 | strong, but both scale with how many EVs a country has |
| chargers per 1,000 EVs vs EV sales share | 42 | 0.09 | 0.565 | no relationship: high adopters do NOT have more chargers per EV |
| YoY charger growth vs YoY EV stock growth (country-years, 2011-2025) | 394 | 0.30 | 6.8e-10 | weak (Pearson r = 0.05) |

Charger growth in year t-k vs EV stock growth in year t: lag 0y: rho 0.30 (n = 394); lag 1y: rho 0.18 (n = 353); lag 2y: rho 0.09 (n = 312)

Reading: countries with more chargers do have more EVs, but the relationship is about scale. Per EV, high-adoption countries do not have more chargers (Norway: 97% share with about 35 EVs per public charger). The data support an association, not a causal 'build chargers and EVs follow' claim.

## 5. H3: is growth concentrated in a handful of markets?
- EV car stock growth 2020-2025 across 55 markets: 63.5M cars
- Top 5: China 62.3%, United States 9.4%, Germany 3.9%, United Kingdom 3.3%, France 2.8% = 81.8% (top 10: 87.6%)
- Gini 0.870, HHI 0.402 (above 0.25 = highly concentrated)
- Market size (2020 stock) vs growth: Spearman 0.88; 2020 penetration vs growth: 0.46; penetration vs growth controlling for size: partial rho -0.39 (p = 0.012, n = 42)
- Reading: growth concentrates in LARGE markets; once size is accounted for, already-saturated markets (e.g. Norway) grow less.
